61.changes: Already a modern, food-safe Caesar: mayo-based dressing (no raw egg), anchovy-garlic paste, Dijon and lemon match current best-practice versions exactly. Nothing worth changing.

sources: USDA FoodSafety.gov poultry minimum internal temperature guidance

86.changes: Use room-temperature cream cheese for an even base layer, and microwave in short 30-second bursts, stirring between, rather than straight through, so the cheese doesn't turn rubbery.

87.changes: No oven temperature is given for the 20+5-10 minute bake. Modern versions of this layered dip bake at 350°F; add that so results aren't left to oven guesswork.

101.changes: Let the mixed sauce rest in the fridge 30-60 minutes before serving; modern cocktail sauce recipes note this melds the horseradish and Worcestershire noticeably better.

105.changes: No changes; blanch-and-shock technique, toasted walnuts, and a make-ahead vinaigrette already match how Bon Appetit and current green-bean-and-blue-cheese recipes are still made.

107.changes: No changes; toothpick doneness test and creaming method are already current technique. Spice level is mild versus modern gingerbread but reflects a distinct colonial style — leave it.

109.changes: No changes needed; the family's own note already specifies real margarine over butter deliberately, and doneness/mixing technique matches modern blondie recipes. Leave as is.

116.changes: No changes needed; boil-mill-cook technique and sugar ratio already match how modern jellied cranberry sauce is made. A durable, correct method.

129.changes: No changes needed; patting cucumber slices dry before spreading already addresses the main failure point (sogginess) that modern versions of this canape also flag.

134.changes: Toast the curry powder in a dry pan 30-60 seconds before mixing into the dressing; raw curry powder tastes dusty, and this is now standard technique in well-regarded curried chicken salads.

135.changes: No changes needed; cooking to a measured 175°F already clears the USDA safe threshold for egg custards (160°F) and beats vaguer 'cook until done' instructions in older recipes.

136.changes: Technique already matches modern guidance: pull at a slight jiggle, letting carryover finish it. Optional refinement: confirm doneness with an instant-read thermometer at about 200°F center instead of judging by eye alone.

139.changes: Frying temp (360-370°F) and multi-turn technique already match modern cake-doughnut guidance (King Arthur: 365-375°F, minimal handling, three flips). Nothing to change; clip a thermometer to the pot to hold temp steady.

141.changes: Egg-cream ratio and 375°F/35-40min bake already match modern quiche lorraine. Add a doneness cue: pull when the center still jiggles slightly and rest 10-15 minutes; baking to a fixed time risks rubbery texture.

155.changes: Cooks' note already fixes the recipe's real flaw (cook potatoes separately). Franey's timing and method otherwise match modern versions of this dish closely; nothing else here is worth changing.

164.changes: Custard is egg-thin (half an egg per 2 slices, no cream) versus richer modern ratios. Use closer to one egg per 2 slices with a splash of cream and slightly stale bread for custardy centers.

167.changes: Only 16 oz vinegar acidifies a huge batch of low-acid pears, peaches, onions and peppers plus tomatoes — an untested ratio for safe water-bath canning. Add bottled lemon juice per jar or check pH first.

169.changes: Crisco-and-chocolate method is sound; keep it as-is. "Bake 20-30 minutes" is vague — use a toothpick with a few moist crumbs as the doneness cue instead of time alone, to avoid dry, overbaked squares.

170.changes: Canned beef broth is already salted, so the full 2 t. salt risks oversalting; add it in two additions and taste before the last. Otherwise technique (late zucchini, short simmer) matches modern versions well.

174.changes: No cooking involved; recipe is a straight assembly of prepared products (salsa, Bloody Mary mix) as intended. Nothing to change — matches modern gazpacho-shooter recipes.

175.changes: Technique already matches modern glazed-carrot methods (e.g. Ina Garten): cook carrots, then reduce with fat, sugar, and fruit into a glaze. Nothing to change.

183.changes: Shock beans in ice water right after blanching, before buttering, to stop carryover cooking and lock in bright green color — standard step in modern almondine recipes, skipped here.

189.changes: Cook's notes already fixed the main issue (cut the oil, add mayonnaise to stabilize the dressing). Nothing further to change; the rest of the recipe is sound as written.

192.changes: USDA's poultry minimum has been 165°F since 2006; roasting breast meat to 170°F overcooks and dries it. Pull at 160°F and rest — carryover finishes it safely and juicier.

195.changes: Recipe already matches the modern Washington Post technique almost verbatim: roux, milk, cheese melted in off heat, buttered-crumb top. Nothing to change.

196.changes: Chill the assembled pastry-wrapped brie 15-20 min before baking so it puffs evenly instead of slumping or leaking, and cut a small steam vent in the top. Chill runs during oven preheat.

199.changes: Technique already avoids the classic error of boiling milk (which scorches it and forms a skin) — only the water-chocolate base boils; milk is just warmed. Nothing to change.

200.changes: Add a squeeze of lemon juice and a pinch of Old Bay or paprika; canned crab reads flat without the acid and spice every modern hot crab dip uses. Fresh lump crab if available.

201.changes: Cooks_note confirms it already matches ATK's method (oil then butter, 1.5 min per side, translucent center); this is the current standard sear technique. Nothing to change.

202.changes: No-bake icebox assembly with no technique or safety concern; using full-fat (not light) Cool Whip is already the right call for structure. Nothing to change.

258.changes: Bloom the cumin with the onion in the fat before adding the broth, rather than dropping it in with the liquid; releases more of its flavor.

266.changes: Nothing to change. Cooks' notes already record two successful tests, the second with syrup amounts already tuned; the recipe is proven and shouldn't be altered further.

287.changes: Use full-fat block cream cheese and creamy commercial peanut butter, not natural/separated, for a smooth sliceable filling; let cream cheese soften to room temp first so it beats lump-free.

364.changes: Nothing to fix; separating eggs and folding whipped whites in is already the technique modern Norwegian waffle recipes use. A milk batter without cardamom is a valid regional variant.

365.changes: No changes beyond the family's own note, which already settles the noodle-layer question. Boiling regular lasagna noodles and folding raw egg into the cheese mix is standard technique.

376.changes: This is essentially the classic deviled-ham/spam-spread style (grated meat plus tangy dressing), distinct from smoother modern versions; Miracle Whip's tang suits it. No fix needed.

396.changes: This matches Pace's own classic cream-cheese-and-picante recipe closely; technique and make-ahead handling are already correct. Nothing to change.

409.changes: Baking soda for acidity is validated by modern testing, not an outdated trick — keep it. Bloom the tomato paste with the sauteed onion/garlic/celery for 1-2 minutes before adding tomatoes to deepen flavor.

410.changes: Canned condensed soup as the binder is still standard in comparable modern layered tortilla bakes, not a compromise to fix. Nothing here is wrong, unsafe, or outdated enough to change.

420.changes: 3:1 oil-to-vinegar with mustard as emulsifier, shaken not whisked, already matches the standard modern vinaigrette method exactly. Nothing to change.

465.changes: The untested 2026 revision already matches current best practice: baking-soda dry brine, oil-bloomed spices, post-sear acid, ~120F pull all align with modern shrimp-grilling guidance. No further change indicated.

474.changes: Typical carryover for a steak rested away from heat is only about 5-10F per reverse-sear references, far below your +33F, supporting your hypothesis that radiant heat or probe placement caused the spike, not normal carryover.

8.changes: Sweetness complaints are real, but the author warns cutting sugar sacrifices the crisp edge — leave as is. Watch closely near the 12-min mark; convection ovens especially risk burnt undersides before the center sets.

23.changes: Cook's own 7/2018 note confirms the oven method works well with tenderloin, basted before roasting. If ever made with a larger 9-lb loin, tent with foil near the end — the sauce can scorch during extended roasting, per one reader.

48.changes: Your own notes (repeated across 4 years) already flag this as under-thickened — add more flour to the beurre manié, matching readers who separately call the soup thin. Multiple commenters also say it needs noticeably more salt.

96.changes: Toss the croutons with smashed garlic along with the oil before baking — the most experienced commenter's (40 batches) fix for more flavor. Whisk the dressing by hand; a food processor risks turning the olive oil bitter, per reader caution.

172.changes: The recipe's 1–3 min blanch reliably overcooks the broccolini into mush — the dominant, repeated complaint among readers. Cut the blanch to about 1 minute, or skip it and sauté directly in the garlic oil, then cover briefly to steam.

176.changes: Independent reports 14 years apart find 5 eggs makes the dough too runny, yielding flat puffs — use 4 eggs and slightly less cheese. Bake to deep golden-brown, not just golden; underbaked puffs collapse as they cool.

230.changes: Your 6/2020 note found this mild — the outside seasoning never reaches the flesh. Salt the fish 20+ minutes before grilling (dry-brine, passive wait) and consider the pellet smoker instead of gas for more smoke flavor.

237.changes: The recipe's single dark rum already sidesteps the disputed white-rum-base debate. Choose a full-bodied aged rum (commenters favor Jamaican-style) over a light one — the recurring authenticity complaint is that a thin rum flattens the drink.

306.changes: The 'too salty' complaint (1 Tbs. for 3 potatoes) carries a 2-helpful/10-unhelpful vote split — readers largely reject it, so leave the salt as written. The one useful tip: rösti can be made ahead and reheated.

326.changes: Multiple readers blame convection for the dry results your temping already guards against — run bake mode, fan off. Your 12/23 idea to rub paste under the skin too is reader-confirmed as an improvement.

357.changes: Your 10/23 note flagged it as a bit sweet — cut brown sugar from 3 Tbs to about 1.5, matching a reader's successful cut to 1 Tbs. Sear on your high-output burner for real color.

375.changes: Your 4/22 note found the emulsion never came together; readers separately call it oily too — cut the 2/3 cup oil slightly. Add lemon juice gradually and taste; readers report '2 lemons' swings from balanced to overpowering.
